anya (product): Heads-up — I'm proposing an "alert gating" concept for SLO alerts surfaced in the console. Goal: give teams an explicit pre-notify tier that shows noisy signals in the UI but doesn't push to pager until crossing a stricter gate. Thoughts?

sam (eng-platform): Nice. So like 'info' -> 'warn' -> 'page' tiers, but with console-only visibility for the first tier?

carlos (sre): Exactly. We need a way to surface low-confidence regressions so owners can triage before they escalate. Current pager flood comes from noisy per-tenant blasts.

kevin (devex): UX Q: how does this map to our notify API? Do we add a boolean like "suppress_until_gate" or a separate "gating_level"? Need to keep SDK ergonomic.

anya (product): Proposal: add "gating_level": ["log","console","pager"] and a separate "confidence_score" float. Console shows "console" alerts with a small badge and quick actions.

sam (eng-platform): Implementation note: routing policies already accept escalation tiers. We could reuse that but need per-tenant overrides and a signal smoothing window. Also rate-limits must still apply to console views.

liz (pm): Can we add a hover tooltip explaining why something is in "console" vs "pager"? Non-SLO-savvy product teams ask this all the time.

carlos (sre): Also important: the fallback behavior. If a tenant has a high error-rate, do we auto-promote console items to pager after X mins or if volume > Y? Need SRE-defined defaults.

kevin (devex): For SDKs/console we should keep the API payload compact. Example shape: 
```json
{
  "policy": "latency_p99",
  "threshold": 1200,
  "gating_level": "console",
  "confidence_score": 0.62,
  "auto_promote_minutes": 15
}
```
This could be the new notify payload.

sam (eng-platform): Backend concerns: auto-promotion interacts with existing quota-based routing. If we promote for too many tenants at once, Dedicated pools will spike. Need a global circuit-breaker and a circuit priority metric.

anya (product): Good call. I'm thinking default auto_promote_minutes = 10 and an opt-out at tenant-level. We'll also expose a per-tenant "quiet window" preference in the console.

carlos (sre): Also add a per-tenant mute button that creates a soft-snooze with expiration and a reason field. That should be in the audit logs.

kevin (devex): For the console UI: quick actions (Acknowledge / Promote / Snooze / View history). Acknowledge shouldn't stop console items from auto-promoting unless you explicitly snooze.

sam (eng-platform): On the API side, we'll add a new query param to the alerts list: "include_gated=true" so SDKs can opt to fetch console-only alerts. Default remains false for performance.

alert-bot: deploy:alert-routing-service v3.2.1 started rolling (canary=2/10)

carlos (sre): Heads-up — if canary touches routing logic we should hold on big policy changes until it's stable. Can we gate the rollout on canary success?

sam (eng-platform): Will do, will also add an integration test simulating 500 tenants with mixed gating levels.

anya (product): Next steps: I’ll draft a mock in Figma, kevin can prototype SDK payloads, sam will scope infra work, carlos will define SRE defaults for auto-promote and global circuit-breaker. Back here end of week for sign-off. :thumbsup:
